_comment: Zenodo deposition metadata (legacy REST format: PUT /api/deposit/depositions/<id> with this object as the body, or enter the fields in the web form). Written by tools/build_zenodo_metadata.py (numbers: metadata_numbers.json); do not edit by hand. No `grants` (NSF 2608825 is not in Zenodo's awards database): enter the funding as a custom award, see ZENODO_FUNDING_MANUAL.md. publication_date is set by Zenodo at publication. DOI placeholders 10.5281/zenodo.PENDING-<name> are replaced by tools/zenodo_release.py writeback.

metadata.title: ORCHID-Registry: phase registry of binary systems
metadata.description:
ORCHID-Registry: phase registry of binary systems, version 0: one entry per phase of each binary system, with every name the phase goes by, the CALPHAD models that describe it, where calculated phase diagrams make it stable, example literature references, and a crystal-structure type assigned only when certain. Part of the ORCHID data release v2026.10. Short name in the paper: Registry.

What

  • phases/registry.json: compact index (id, system, names, structure tier and prototype, counts) of 10,430 phases in 1,241 binary systems, with the full records (models with TDB definitions, stability, references) in phases/systems/<SYS>.json; id phase:<sorted elements>:<slug> (the SGTE-corpus canonical convention). Names in namespaces tdb (TDB file and phase name), paper (DOI and printed label), corpus, mp, oqmd: 43,190 names.
  • Models: 22,556 TDB phase declarations (file SHA-256, sublattices, site ratios, constituents) from the bundled SGTE binary collection; stability ranges per calculated diagram; literature value counts; up to 10 example references per phase (assessments first) with DOI and role.
  • Structure: 6,228 phases assigned from the standard phase name (tier A), 154 from a unique Materials Project + OQMD on-hull match (tier B, "DFT-supported"), 1,248 assessment-declared (tier C, assessor-stated: exactly one consistent structure in the Hallstedt 2025 crystallographic table for that phase name and system), 1,304 liquid and 231 gas; 1,236 phases carry review candidates and are marked needs_review.
  • phases/structure_types.json: 1,563 structure types (prototype, Strukturbericht, Pearson symbol, space group), each with its source; also structure_types.csv and structure_types.parquet; registry.csv, registry.parquet, registry.jsonld (schema.org DefinedTermSet), review_queue.json, CONFLICTS.md, SCHEMA.md.

How

Deterministic builder (tools/build_phase_registry.py, standard library) over the bundled TDB files, the Hallstedt 2025 crystallographic table, the ORCHID SGTE-corpus phase mappings and literature values, the calculated binary phase diagrams and the Materials Project / OQMD hull layers. No model or network calls.

Limitations

  • A structure type is assigned only when certain or, for tier C, as stated by the assessment's crystallographic table; everything else is a review candidate, not a claim.
  • DFT entries are computed 0 K structures, not the CALPHAD phase; tier B requires agreement of both databases and a unique structure type for the space group and stoichiometry.
  • Paper labels come from machine-extracted literature values (Version 1); mapping basis is recorded per name.
  • Binary systems only; stability comes from calculated (not measured) diagrams.

Licence

ORCHID's data are released under CC BY 4.0, as are the SGTE (B. Hallstedt, Calphad 89 (2025) 102833), Materials Project and OQMD data from which they are derived; attributions and statements of changes are in NOTICE.md, the licence of each folder in LICENSES.md (both in the bundle).

Files: one zip (orchid-phase-registry-v2026.10.zip) holding the files at their repository paths, a MANIFEST.sha256, the README, CHANGELOG and licence files. Its file list with sizes and SHA-256 is zenodo/phase-registry.files.json in the data repository.

How to cite

R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID-Registry: phase registry of binary systems (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.PENDING-phase-registry

Part of: R. Arróyave, J. Saal, D. Shin, ORCHID data: umbrella record of the ORCHID datasets (version 2026.10; Version 1, machine-extracted), Zenodo (2026). https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.PENDING-orchid-data

Also cite B. Hallstedt, The SGTE collection of binary datasets, Calphad 89 (2025) 102833, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.calphad.2025.102833 (CC BY 4.0), and the original assessment named in each file; A. Jain et al., The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation, APL Materials 1 (2013) 011002, https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4812323 (CC BY 4.0); J. E. Saal et al., JOM 65 (2013) 1501, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11837-013-0755-4 and S. Kirklin et al., npj Comput. Mater. 1 (2015) 15010, https://doi.org/10.1038/npjcompumats.2015.10 (CC BY 4.0); the original source of every value you use (paper_citation / paper_doi, and cited_dois for values the paper cites from earlier work).

Version 1, machine-extracted: values were read from papers by language-model readers constrained to quote their source and checked automatically (quote verification, field-placement rule, printed-page sign checks, DFT and Kim et al. 2017 cross-checks); a hand-checked precision sample is in progress.
